newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Third consortium seeks Singapore telecom licence.
newsitem.headline: Third consortium seeks Singapore telecom licence.

text.p: A third consortium said on Friday it would enter the race for the one or two licences to run basic telecommunications services which Singapore plans to issue next year.
Marine-based conglomerate SembCorp Ltd, state-owned railway Singapore MRT (SMRT) and WorldCom Inc of the United States said they would make a joint bid a licence to start services in 2000.
SembCorp and SMRT said in March they might bid for a licence that would allow them to provide a fixed telephone service to rival the current local monopoly, Singapore Telecommunications Ltd.
On Friday, a joint statement said SembCorp and SMRT would together hold 65 percent of the bidding venture, with WorldCom holding the remaining 35 percent.
Two other consortiums have also said they will bid for a domestic licence.
Analysts say that on paper, the stronger is the combination of British Telecom, Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp, state utility Singapore Power and state-owned Singapore Technologies Telemedia.
The other is from Britain's Cable & Wireless, HongKong Telecommunications Ltd, Singapore Press Holdings and Keppel Telecom.
The new bidder's statement said on Friday the three companies in its group were a strong combination.
It said SembCorp's Pacific Internet had proved a competitive Internet Service Provider (ISP) and that the parent company had extensive experience in infrastructure projects.
SMRT's tunnel and viaduct network throughout the island would provide ideal routes for cabling and the company already had a fibre-optic network for its own communications, the statement said.
It said WorldCom, one of the four largest long-distance telecommunications companies in the United States, had extensive experience of setting up networks at home and in Europe.
SembCorp chairman Philip Yeo promised a state-of-the-art service if the consortium won a licence.

"Our vision is to develop a state-of-the-art telecommunications infrastructure and provide the best services at competitive prices without compromise on the quality of service," the statement quoted him as saying.
